title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; 1-day closure in 7-day week; no prior closure data, but similar closures in retail reduce weekly sales by 10–15% on average. No evidence of stockpiling.

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Two recent price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) at same level produced no lift; noise-adjusted promotion effects are x1.0. Price increase likely reduces demand slightly.

adjustment.analysis: The target week has no event or promotion, but a price increase of 3.4% and a store closure on Monday. Price increases typically reduce demand; past price hikes (2026-09-28, 2026-10-05) showed no lift, and the 2025-02-17 30% off promotion had only a 5% lift (noise-adjusted x1.0). The store closure on Monday likely reduces sales by ~10–15% (1-day closure in a 7-day week). No prior closure effect is available, so the adjustment is conservative. The classical model suggests no uplift, consistent with weak past promotion effects. The baseline already reflects seasonal trends (mean_52=6.3, trend_13=34%), so no seasonal ramp is needed. Median multiplier adjusted downward for closure. Spreads unchanged.

brief:
PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 11.0 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 9.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
